target_customer: Software engineering teams that run CI/CD and want an autonomous agent to handle CI failures, flaky tests, slow builds and code review
problem: Engineers spend time on CI failures, flaky tests and release problems. Existing tooling creates alerts and dashboards but developers still do the work.
business_model: B2B SaaS for engineering teams, with a pricing page and early access
product_category: AI DevOps and platform engineering agent

founders.name: Sam Alba
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page and mendral.com. Dagger outcome not checked.

founders.name: Andrea Luzzardi
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page says he helped write Docker's earliest code. Roles from mendral.com.

exit.reason: The team joined Anthropic to work on Claude Platform and the hosted Mendral product is being discontinued, per the company's own post. The New Stack calls it an acqui-hire. Terms not disclosed.

competitors.name: CircleCI Chunk
competitors.what: AI agent that detects flaky tests and generates fixes
competitors.traction_then: Beta, no extra charge during beta

technical_complexity.rationale: An agent that diagnoses CI failures and ships fixes across arbitrary repos needs reliable tool use, log understanding and safe code changes. The founders had deep Docker and Dagger CI experience.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with customer CI gives some stickiness but foundation-model vendors and CI platforms could ship similar agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CircleCI shipped a flaky-test agent in 2025. The team was absorbed by Anthropic on 2026-07-21 rather than being copied out of the market.

market_need_then: Launch post claimed CI/CD in production for 15 teams, 5 paying, including PostHog. The site names Metabase, Luminai and Clipboard Health as customers. Flaky CI is a long-running developer complaint.

branding.domain_note: Owns mendral.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Product mockups of PR reviews and Sentry or Slack threads
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, direct, sentence-case, developer-focused (Platform Engineering on Autopilot)

branding.brand_signature: Credibility from the Docker and Dagger founders

brand_strength.rationale: Clear developer voice and trademark filings in September 2025 (USPTO listing), but no press about the brand itself and a short life.

outcome_analysis: Two repeat founders from Docker and Dagger launched in the winter 2026 batch, reached 15 teams with 5 paying within months and raised a small pre-seed style YC note and a March 2026 seed from Pioneer Fund. On 2026-07-21 the team joined Anthropic and the hosted product was wound down. This is a team-led landing rather than a product outcome, which is why it is tagged as an acqui-hire.
notes: The seed rests on PitchBook only (undisclosed amount, 11 March 2026, Pioneer Fund). The 500K note rests on CB Insights only and matches YC's standard deal size, so stage is other; Mendral's blog says YC invested a second time. VCBacked also lists Toloka.vc, Rebel Fund and Outlier Grove; an aggregator total of $15M and a founding year of 2023 conflict with other sources and are unverified. The exit type acquisition is labelled an acqui-hire by The New Stack and the product was shut down; YC directory status is Inactive.
